test_title: RRB ALP CBT-II (Heat Engine) Official Paper (Held On 06 May, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is the reason that cam lobe causes the engine to make a ticking or tapping noise, especially when idling, and is often rhythmic and varies in loudness?

options.text: When the cam lobe is subjected to higher load.
When the cam lobe is hot.
When the cam lobe wears out.
When cam lobe is has insufficient lubrication.

solution:
The correct answer is __When the cam lobe wears out.__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Cam lobe wear__ is a common cause of ticking or tapping noises in the engine.
 
• When the cam lobe wears out, it affects the valve timing and lift, leading to irregular engine operation.
 
• This wear can cause a rhythmic ticking noise that varies in loudness, especially noticeable when idling.
 
• Insufficient lubrication or the presence of debris can accelerate cam lobe wear.
 
• Regular maintenance and timely oil changes are essential to prevent excessive wear.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

 
• **Insufficient Lubrication:**

 
 
• Cam lobes rely on proper lubrication to prevent wear and damage.
 
• Low oil levels or degraded oil can result in insufficient lubrication, leading to noise.
 
 
 
• **Higher Load:**
 
 
• Excessive load on the engine can increase wear on the cam lobes.
 
• However, this is less likely to cause rhythmic ticking compared to cam lobe wear.
 
 
 
• **Heat Effects:**
 
 
• High temperatures can thin the oil, reducing its lubricating properties.
 
• This may indirectly contribute to cam lobe wear over time.
